channel.title: Headroom Studio - Notes from the studio
channel.description: Notes on monitor level, hearing dose, loudness delivery and the Mac apps behind them.

item.title: Switching speakers at a calibrated level
item.description: Each speaker pair needs its own monitor level to play at the same SPL. Audita measures it per pair, Lyra 1.9 recalls it with the switch, and the workflow now runs on second-generation Universal Audio Volt interfaces too.

item.title: macOS 27: new icons, real glass, and an input that measured nothing
item.description: Lyra 1.8, Audita 1.5 and Specula 1.3 are ready for macOS 27. What the update took: Icon Composer icons that need a second Xcode, a volume pill matched to the system's glass one blur value at a time, and an input device that went silent on 27 until the log said why.

item.title: Audita 1.4: absolute SPL from a UMIK-1 serial number
item.description: Audita 1.4 reads measurement-mic calibration files, and on a miniDSP UMIK-1 it takes absolute SPL straight from the factory file you fetch by serial number. Includes the 30 dB detour that got the conversion right, live input-volume compensation, a calibration health card, and a rig self-check.

item.title: Specula 1.2: custom loudness targets and raw PCM import
item.description: Specula 1.2 adds custom loudness targets - your delivery spec as a first-class compliance target - and raw PCM import for headerless audio under a declared format, in the app and on the CLI. Free update for existing licenses.

item.title: Specula 1.1: spectral editing, Record mode, an Audio Unit chain and a signal generator
item.description: Specula 1.1 adds spectral editing on the analysis spectrogram, Record mode with live BS.1770 meters, an Audio Unit chain in Edit mode, and a signal generator. Free update for existing licenses.

item.title: Why streaming TV loudness is measured on the dialogue
item.description: Netflix, Prime Video, Apple TV+, Disney+ and HBO Max all specify -27 LKFS dialogue-gated. Measure the whole programme instead and the number can be off by more than 10 dB.

item.title: Per-chapter loudness for audiobook delivery
item.description: An audiobook can pass on the whole-file loudness number and still fail chapter by chapter. Per-chapter RMS, deviation from the book's own median, and the three ACX gates - measured before you upload.

item.title: Measuring the ACX noise floor
item.description: ACX measures the noise floor on the room tone between phrases. Specula finds the speech with a voice-activity detector and reads the floor only over the gaps, live, so the passage that fails is visible before upload.

item.title: Wiring Lyra into every Mac automation surface
item.description: App Intents, Focus Filters, x-callback URLs. One change underneath, several different shapes on top.

item.title: The musician tinnitus number is 43%
item.description: A 2026 meta-analysis of 28,000+ musicians puts hard numbers on tinnitus, hearing loss and hyperacusis. No genre is safer.

item.title: Pairing Audita and Lyra
item.description: Audita measures the SPL at the listening position and writes it into one of Lyra's three Reference Level slots. From then on Ctrl+F11 recalls a monitor level with its dB SPL figure attached.

item.title: The 3 dB rule - how loudness halves safe listening time
item.description: Every 3 dB increase halves the safe listening time and every 3 dB decrease doubles it. The NIOSH table, the OSHA 5 dB figure and where it came from, and what the rule says about a mixing day.

item.title: The case for calibrated studio monitoring
item.description: Set the monitor level against a measured SPL once and come back to it. Why mixes translate better that way, where the cinema, K-System and broadcast references put the number, and a three-level setup on the F-keys.
